children: Nuclear energy companies are continuing to seek public listings, despite Standard Nuclear
and Amazon-backed
X-Energy
, which both went public earlier this year, trading below their IPO prices.
Newcleo

is the latest to go public, with the European company making its U.S. market debut on Tuesday following a SPAC merger. Meanwhile, Westinghouse Electric, which is owned by Brookfield Renewable Partners
and Cameco
, is reportedly eyeing an IPO for later this year.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
, and Michael Del Monte which nuclear energy stocks they favored right now.

Manika Premsingh: Nuclear energy might have had a poor year so far in the stock market, but make no mistake, its future is full of potential. The correction follows a massive rally in recent years as the sector became the preferred energy provider for Big Tech's huge projected AI demands. In addition, policy around the world has been strongly supportive of nuclear energy as a reliable supplier of clean energy. With many nuclear energy stocks still pre-operational, such as reactor developers and uranium miners, a keener judgment than usual is called for when investing in the sector.

The most straightforward route to promising returns with limited downside is investing in companies with proven operational capabilities, sound financials, and at least long-term potential for price upside. The final criterion is important, as even the correction year-to-date hasn't been enough to reduce valuations to attractive levels at this time.
For the longer term, I would pick the Canadian uranium miner Cameco
and the nuclear components producer BWX Technologies
, both of which have strong credentials, are industry leaders, and have the potential to double over the next five years.
(Manika Premsingh leads the SA investing group Green Growth Giants.)

Mike Zaccardi: There remains concern among AI-adjacent names right now, following the mid-year momentum unwind. Currently, I'd stick with more conservative, diversified players, such as NextEra Energy

What's also frustrating for investors is that clean energy has quietly been under significant selling pressure, contributing to the broader decline in nuclear power stocks. Higher interest rates are another clear headwind.
I believe solid buying opportunities will emerge in Q4, but it might first require a high-volatility sell-off to clear out weak hands.
Don Beynon: The most attractive pure play nuclear stock is Cameco

. CCJ has one of the best uranium resources/mines in the world, along with nuclear fuel cycle facilities in conversion, fuel fabrication, and enrichment research. CCJ also owns 49% of Westinghouse, the world leader in nuclear plant design, fuel fabrication, and nuclear services.
Michael Del Monte: I think GE Vernova
, which I hold, is the best-positioned company in the nuclear industry, given the company's diversified power and electrification portfolio.

While nuclear has gained significant interest in recent years with the hyperscalers securing long-term agreements for power capacity, I believe meaningful adoption will take time due to the complexity of the nuclear fuel cycle. GE Vernova will continue to capitalize on natural gas turbine demand while benefiting from the long-term transition to nuclear.
ExxonMobil

, which I also hold, may also be an appealing strategy, given the company's investments in graphite extraction. ExxonMobil will capitalize on hydrocarbons while gradually transitioning into new energy production.
The basis for these picks is that both investments remove the long-duration risk of an energy transition.
